Get the metadata carried by a result

Source: R/meta.R
gcd_meta.Rd

Every tibble from gcd_rows() carries the response's metadata as an attribute: what the rows are, where they come from and how to cite them. gcd_meta() returns it.

Many dplyr verbs drop attributes, so read the metadata from the result as it came back. gcd_citation() also accepts a dataset name.

Usage

gcd_meta(x)

Arguments

x

A tibble returned by gcd_rows().

Value

A named list: dataset (the name), title, detail, key_metric, units (a named list of each metric's unit), null_semantics (what a missing value means), source, source_url, citation, license, schema (the schema's path), advisories (a tibble of code and message), year_meaning, omitted_columns (columns left out because they were empty), data_version, updated_at and request_url. Fields the API didn't send are absent.

See also

gcd_citation() to cite the data.

Other utilities: gcd_cache_clear(), gcd_citation()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
grad <- gcd_rows("graduation_rate_4_year_cohort", district = "Fulton County",
                 year = 2024, demographic = "all")
gcd_meta(grad)$advisories
}
